title: Smallest-degree Keller counterexamples in dimension 3
W: In 2026 the Jacobian conjecture was shown false in dimension 3: there are polynomial maps C^3 -> C^3 with constant nonzero Jacobian that are not invertible, and the known examples have degree 7. Decide whether such a map can have degree at most 4. More generally, find the smallest degree a counterexample in dimension 3 can have.
M: Let $d_3=\min\{\deg F: F\in\mathbb C[x,y,z]^3,\ \det DF\in\mathbb C^\times,\ F\notin\mathrm{Aut}(\mathbb C^3)\}$, where $\deg F=\max_i\deg F_i$. By Wang's theorem $d_3\ge3$, and the 2026 examples (Alp\"oge; van den Essen) give $d_3\le7$. Decide whether $d_3\le4$, i.e. whether every Keller map $\mathbb C^3\to\mathbb C^3$ of degree $\le4$ is an automorphism. Ultimately, determine $d_3$.
why: Once the Jacobian conjecture failed in dimension 3, the natural next question is where exactly it fails. The minimal degree of a counterexample tells us how far the classical positive results (Wang for degree 2, the reductions to cubic maps) can be pushed in a fixed dimension, and a degree-3 or degree-4 counterexample would bear on the cubic-homogeneous reduction.
issues: The original M asked to PROVE degree <=4 Keller maps on C^3 are automorphisms. In this period the Jacobian conjecture has been refuted in dimension 3 (Alpöge, July 2026; van den Essen's elementary version has component degrees 7,6,4; Gao/Gallagher families; Isabelle/AFP formal verification). The degree-<=4 case does not appear settled in what I found, but its truth value is now unclear, so the statement was changed from 'prove' to 'decide', with the minimal degree d_3 as the real target. Not checked: whether some of the newer families (Gallagher H_d, Gao) already reach polynomial degree <=6 or <=5; their papers mostly report geometric degree (fibre size), not polynomial degree. Whether degree-3 maps in dimension 3 are settled classically is also unverified, so d_3>=3 is the only safe lower bound.

title: Drum tones of superellipses
W: Take the region |x|^p + |y|^p <= r^p, scaled to have area 1. At p = 2 it is a disk, which has the lowest possible bass note of any region of that area (Faber–Krahn). As p grows to infinity it becomes a square, whose note is higher. Show that the note rises steadily the whole way from p = 2 to infinity.
M: For $p\in[2,\infty)$ let $D_p=\{(x,y):|x|^p+|y|^p\le r_p^p\}$ with $r_p$ chosen so that $|D_p|=1$, and let $\lambda_1(p)$ be the first Dirichlet eigenvalue of $-\Delta$ on $D_p$. Prove that $\lambda_1$ is strictly increasing on $[2,\infty)$, with $\lambda_1(2)=\pi j_{0,1}^2$ and $\lambda_1(p)\uparrow2\pi^2$ as $p\to\infty$.
why: This is a test case for how the Dirichlet eigenvalue moves along a natural one-parameter family of convex sets joining the Faber–Krahn minimiser (the disk) to the square. Monotonicity along such families is a known hard type of question in shape optimisation, since Hadamard's formula gives the derivative but not its sign.
issues: I computed it with the method of particular solutions, using a D4-symmetric Fourier–Bessel basis. The area-normalised lambda_1 comes out at 18.168 (p=2), 18.262 (2.5), 18.431 (3), 18.752 (4), 18.991 (5), 19.159 (6), 19.367 (8), 19.482 (10), 19.614 (15), 19.666 (20), 19.727 (50), heading up to 2pi^2 = 19.739. It is cleanly increasing, so the conjecture looks true, with no counterexample. I found no literature on this exact family, so it is novel but narrow. A proof via Hadamard's shape derivative would need sign information on |du/dn|^2 tested against the normal velocity of the boundary, which looks technical rather than deep. I added the endpoint values to M. The p in [1,2] side (where the shape tends to the rotated square at p=1) is a natural companion question.

title: Irrationality of the quartic oscillator ground state
W: The lowest energy of the quartic oscillator, -d^2/dx^2 + x^4 on the line, is about 1.0603620905. Show that it is irrational.
M: Let $E_0=\min\sigma\big(-\tfrac{d^2}{dx^2}+x^4\big)$, the operator taken self-adjoint on $L^2(\mathbb R)$ ($E_0=1.06036209048418\ldots$). Prove that $E_0\notin\mathbb Q$.
why: Irrationality and transcendence are known for spectral data of exactly solvable problems, such as Bessel zeros via Siegel's theorem. For a genuinely non-solvable Schrödinger operator, apparently nothing is known. Voros's exact WKB and spectral-determinant functional relations describe E_0 implicitly, so a proof would have to turn those relations, or a series or continued fraction for E_0, into Diophantine information.
issues: The numerical value is correct. I found no literature on the arithmetic nature of E_0; it is novel in the sense of never having been posed explicitly. The statement is precise. There is no realistic route: no available tool gives irrationality of a constant defined only implicitly through a non-solvable ODE. So this is a clean 'benchmark of ignorance' rather than an attackable problem, and the specific choice of x^4 and of E_0 is somewhat arbitrary. Graded B for cleanness, kept below A because it is likely hopeless and not tied to a broader programme.

title: Graceful labellings of forests
W: A forest with m edges and c trees has m + c vertices. Label them with 0, 1, ..., m + c - 1, each label used once, so that the m edge differences |label(u) - label(v)| are all different. Show that every forest has such a labelling. The case 'a tree plus one isolated vertex' already says that every tree can be labelled gracefully if one spare label is allowed.
M: Prove that every forest $F$ with $m$ edges and $c\ge1$ components has a bijection $\ell:V(F)\to\{0,1,\dots,m+c-1\}$ such that the values $|\ell(u)-\ell(v)|$, $uv\in E(F)$, are pairwise distinct. (Key special case: $F=T\sqcup K_1$, i.e. every tree with $m$ edges has an injective labelling into $\{0,\dots,m+1\}$ with distinct edge differences.)
why: Joining the c trees with c - 1 new edges makes a single tree, and a graceful labelling of that tree restricts to such a labelling of the forest. So this statement follows from the Graceful Tree Conjecture (Ringel–Kotzig–Rosa) but is weaker than it. The best unconditional results only give labels in {1,...,(1+eps)n}, or (1-eps)n distinct differences, so even one spare label for every tree would be new progress.
issues: The original hypothesis (c >= 2 and one tree with more than m/2 edges) is arbitrary. An exhaustive backtracking search over ALL forests with at most 11 vertices (475 forests at n=11) found a valid labelling for every one, with or without that hypothesis. So the hypothesis is not doing any work, and I replaced it with 'every forest'. The original version already contains the open T + K1 case (one spare label for every tree), so neither version is easy. Novelty is moderate: range-relaxed graceful labellings are studied (Van Bussel 2002; Adamaszek–Allen–Grosu–Hladký; the 2025 gracesize paper), and I did not find this exact forest formulation, but it is a natural reformulation that experts would likely regard as folklore-adjacent.

title: Sudoku transversals
W: (As posed, the claim is false when the box size n is even.) Corrected version: in every completed Sudoku with an odd box size n (for example 9x9 or 25x25), find a set of cells with exactly one in each row, each column and each symbol.
M: Original claim false for even $n$. Salvaged version: prove that every Sudoku Latin square of order $n^2$ with $n$ odd has a transversal. (This is the case of Ryser's conjecture restricted to Latin squares carrying a Sudoku (gerechte) block structure.)
why: Ryser's conjecture says every Latin square of odd order has a transversal. Montgomery proved that every large Latin square has a partial transversal of size n - 1, but full transversals in odd order remain open. Asking whether the extra Sudoku block structure forces a transversal is a natural, but much narrower, special case.
issues: FALSE as stated. Write n^2 = N and take the Cayley table of Z_N, with entry (i, j) equal to i + sigma(j) mod N, where sigma reorders the columns so that block q of columns holds q, q+n, ..., q+(n-1)n. Each n x n box then holds the sums r*n + t + q + s*n with t, s in {0..n-1}, which are all residues mod N. So every such table is a Sudoku grid, and by construction it is isotopic to the Cayley table of Z_{n^2}. For even n, Z_{n^2} has a nontrivial cyclic Sylow 2-subgroup, so its table has no transversal (Euler for the cyclic case; Hall–Paige in general), and isotopy preserves this. I verified by computer that the n=2 grid is a valid Sudoku with no transversal. For n=3 the same construction is a Sudoku and does have a transversal. With n restricted to odd values, the problem becomes a special case of the open Ryser conjecture with no clear reason why the Sudoku structure should help, so the salvaged version would be C at best.
